clue.text: Elite nags, whipped into shape, run this

definitions.text: Elite nags, whipped into shape, run this

indicators.note: horses whipped into shape are being knocked about, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

parts.note: R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: Top-class horses, trained hard, compete in this famous race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'whipped into shape' rearranges ELITE NAGS into SAINTLEGE; R ends it. The whole clue also defines: the best racehorses run this classic.
explanation.definitionFit: The St Leger is a classic flat race at Doncaster run by the best three-year-old horses.

clue.text: Signs of suffering as Athenian character volunteers to accept budget, finally

indicators.note: to accept says the Greek letter takes another letter into itself

parts.note: sigma is a letter of the Greek alphabet, used in Athens

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of budget

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: A Greek volunteers to take on a final budget, with marks of hardship.
explanation.definitionFit: Stigmata are marks resembling Christ's crucifixion wounds, signs of his suffering.

clue.text: Revolting, like those going bare-chested? That's right!

indicators.note: revolting read as turning over, so the phrase is read backwards

parts.note: people who are bare-chested have no tops on

explanation.surface: Disgusted by people stripping to the waist, someone agrees with a point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolting' looks like disgust but means turning around: NO TOPS read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Spot on is an idiom for exactly correct, an exclamation of agreement.

clue.text: Wimbledon champion, not male

definitions.meaning: Arthur ... won the Wimbledon men's singles in 1975
read as two words, a person not male is a she

explanation.definitionFit: Arthur Ashe, the American tennis player, was Wimbledon singles champion in 1975; and a female is a she.

clue.text: What sustains a setter in trouble again, one constrained by censor

parts.note: to dog someone is to trouble or pursue them
bis is Latin for twice, used to call for a repeat

indicators.note: constrained by says the letter is held within the next word

parts.note: to censor a text is to cut it
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A crossword setter is kept going in difficult times, though held back by a censor.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'setter' is the dog breed, not the puzzle compiler.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog biscuit is the snack that feeds a setter, a breed of gun dog.

clue.text: Are they flowery knickers?

parts.note: the old baggy women's underwear shares its name with things that blossom, so the question plays on both

explanation.definitionFit: Bloomers are loose knee-length knickers, and the word could also mean plants that flower.

clue.text: One replacing good cycling holiday gear

indicators.note: replacing says one letter takes another's place in the word

parts.note: cycling is biking
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A substitute for good cycling gear on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replacing' swaps the G at the end of BIKING for I.
explanation.definitionFit: A bikini is a two-piece swimsuit, typical beach holiday wear.

clue.text: Physicist is a tragic figure losing bet

indicators.note: losing says a run of letters drops out of the word

parts.note: Macbeth is the hero of Shakespeare's tragedy
taken as written

explanation.surface: A scientist is said to be a tragic character who has lost a wager.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernst Mach was an Austrian physicist after whom the speed ratio is named.

clue.text: Opponent finished Old Course

parts.note: someone anti is an opponent of something
past means over, finished

explanation.surface: A rival completed the Old Course, the famous golf links.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old Course' suggests St Andrews golf, but Course is a stage of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Antipasto is the Italian starter, the first course of a meal.

clue.text: Trailblazing traveller left with another identity to tour Italy

indicators.note: to tour means to go around, so the letters wrap around the country's code

parts.note: aka stands for also known as, introducing an alias
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: A pioneering explorer leaves under an alias to travel round Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Laika was the Soviet dog who became the first animal to orbit Earth, a space pioneer.

clue.text: Close to end of condiment that is something put on kipper?

parts.note: nigh means near or close

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of condiment

explanation.surface: Near the end of a sauce, something is added to a smoked herring.
explanation.walkthrough: A kipper is a smoked herring, but here it is someone who kips, sleeps.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightdress is what a sleeper (a kipper, from kip) puts on for bed.

clue.text: Intellectual bachelor loves drunken snog

parts.note: love is nil, O, in tennis, so two loves give two Os

indicators.note: drunken speech slurs the final s sound into sh, changing the kiss

parts.note: snog is British slang for a passionate kiss

explanation.surface: A scholarly single man enjoys an inebriated kiss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunken' slurs KISS into KISH, the final S becoming H.
explanation.definitionFit: Bookish describes someone studious and scholarly, fond of reading.

clue.text: Incline to keep reading and you might well!

definitions.text: Incline to keep reading and you might well!

indicators.note: to keep says the first word holds another letter within it

parts.note: to lean is to incline
R stands for reading, one of the three Rs

explanation.surface: If you tend to keep up your reading, you will acquire knowledge.
explanation.definitionFit: Anyone who keeps up reading will gain knowledge, so the whole clue describes acquiring it.

clue.text: Fibbed half-heartedly, with lies perhaps generating this response

indicators.note: perhaps says the letters might be arranged otherwise
one of the two central letters, half the heart of the word, is dropped

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone told a weak fib, and the lies provoke an incredulous reaction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-heartedly' drops one of the two Bs from FIBBED to give FIBED; 'perhaps' rearranges FIBED plus LIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Disbelief is the natural reaction to hearing fibs and lies, a refusal to credit them.

clue.text: "The Godfather" — major piece of art or utter tedium?

parts.note: the Godfather is the Mafia boss, a don
key means major, most important
a work is a piece of art

explanation.surface: Is The Godfather a masterpiece of film or tedious?
explanation.definitionFit: Donkey work is an idiom for the dull, laborious part of a task.

clue.text: Shakespearean warrior reportedly gave battle wearing ladies' lingerie

indicators.note: reportedly says the phrase is to be heard rather than read

parts.note: gave battle is fought, wearing is in, and ladies' lingerie is bras

explanation.surface: A Shakespearean soldier is said to have fought dressed in women's underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Fortinbras is the Norwegian prince in Hamlet who leads an army.

clue.text: Religious official trying to convert Iraq, so intruding

indicators.note: to convert is to change, so the letters are changed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A churchman tries to convert Iraq by intruding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trying' belongs to the definition: an inquisitor tried heretics.
explanation.definitionFit: The Grand Inquisitor headed the Spanish Inquisition, a church official who tried suspected heretics.

clue.text: Labour's conclusion: party ultimately scorned, getting sent up

indicators.note: sent up in a down entry means the letters are read from the bottom upwards
ultimately picks the last letter of party

parts.note: reviled means scorned, abused

explanation.surface: Labour's party at its end is scorned and mocked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting sent up' reverses Y plus REVILED. Labour is childbirth, not the political party.
explanation.definitionFit: Delivery is the birth of a baby, which ends a mother's labour.

clue.text: Member of oppressive regime thrashed a servant

indicators.note: thrashed means beaten about, so the letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A tyrant's associate beat a servant.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsarevna was a daughter of a tsar, so part of the autocratic Russian ruling family.

clue.text: Call up soldiers, colonel wanting one to get shocking treatment

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, British army soldiers

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the word loses some letters

parts.note: taken as written
ECT is electroconvulsive therapy, treatment by electric shocks

explanation.surface: An officer calls up soldiers, needing one of them to get electric shock therapy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanting' takes the letters O, N, E out of COLONEL, leaving COLL.
explanation.definitionFit: To call something up in the mind is to remember it.

clue.text: Place for better business that's like home inside

indicators.note: inside says the other letters sit within the business abbreviation

parts.note: Co. is the abbreviation for company, a business
as means like
in means at home

explanation.surface: A homely business that feels like home inside.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'better' is one who bets, not an improvement.
explanation.definitionFit: A casino is where gamblers, people who bet, go to wager.

clue.text: More than one counter in taxicab adds the wrong way

indicators.note: the wrong way says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Several meters inside a taxi add up the fare.
explanation.definitionFit: An abacus is a counting frame, and the plural is a set of such counters.

clue.text: American and British foreign affairs

parts.note: to a British newspaper, British things are ours

explanation.surface: The United States and Britain conduct international diplomacy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foreign affairs' sounds diplomatic but means love affairs, called by a French word.
explanation.definitionFit: Amours is a word borrowed from French for love affairs, especially secret ones.

clue.text: After Metamorphoses, Ovid was to issue a denial

indicators.note: Metamorphoses is Ovid's poem of transformations, so the letters are changed

explanation.surface: After writing Metamorphoses, the Roman poet Ovid had to deny something.
explanation.definitionFit: To disavow is to deny responsibility for or knowledge of something.

clue.text: One following pop art movement

indicators.note: following says the next letter comes after the father word

parts.note: pop is an informal word for father, dad
A means one

explanation.surface: An artist follows the Pop Art movement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pop art' looks like one term, but pop is DAD and art belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Dada was an early twentieth-century avant-garde art movement.

clue.text: Unsettled person needing heavy metal, it goes without saying

indicators.note: it goes without says the metal's letters go outside the other piece

parts.note: Pb is the chemical symbol for lead, a heavy metal
a rover is a wanderer, someone with no settled home

explanation.surface: A drifter needs heavy metal music, which goes without saying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it goes without saying' looks like a set phrase, but 'it goes without' is the container and 'saying' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A proverb is a short traditional saying expressing a truth.

clue.text: Winning over with very loud praise

indicators.note: over says the word is turned over, read in reverse

parts.note: up means ahead, winning
ff is fortissimo in music, very loud

explanation.surface: Winning people over with very loud acclaim.
explanation.definitionFit: A puff is an exaggerated piece of praise or publicity.

clue.text: Foreign currency racket completely disheartened auditor

parts.note: a din is a racket, loud noise

indicators.note: with all its inner letters removed, only the ends of the word remain

explanation.surface: Noise from overseas money thoroughly depresses an accountant.
explanation.definitionFit: The dinar is the currency of several countries, including Serbia and Iraq.

clue.text: Judge needs a long time to go over close votes

parts.note: a ref, or referee, judges a match

indicators.note: to go over means to cover, so the period wraps around the next piece

parts.note: an era is a long period of time
end means close, conclusion

explanation.surface: A judge needs ages to review narrow ballots.
explanation.definitionFit: Referenda are public votes on a single question, the plural of referendum.
